material.summary: 基于 Hugo Duprez“代码如泥塑、相信肉眼、喂入参考”方法的 Claude Code 像素特效制作技能：指导 Agent 在 244 个现成特效中检索换色、接入网页或导出精灵表，并通过“多稿起草 → 渲染接触表 → 看图挑刺 → 迭代修整 → 编排 3D 骨骼角色 Act → 自动校验”循环写出媲美手绘的像素特效。
material.install: /plugin marketplace add patch-gg/pixelfx && /plugin install pixelfx@pixelfx；或把 demos/materials/pixelfx-skill/SKILL.md 复制到项目的 .claude/skills/pixelfx/SKILL.md，并在含 tools/ 与 src/ 的工作区（如 demos/materials/pixelfx/source/）中运行。
useCases: 让 Agent 从 244 个现有像素特效中检索、换色（palette）、调参并接入 Canvas/WebGL 游戏
批量或按需将代码像素特效与角色动作导出为 Godot、Unity、Phaser 可读的 Aseprite 精灵表
从零起草全新的纯代码像素特效，通过接触表（contact.png）多轮视觉自检达到手绘像素品质
为缺乏分量的攻击、施法或受击特效补齐蓄力前摇、释放姿态、命中卡肉定格（hit-stop）与受击草靶反应
avoid: 不渲染接触表查看实际画面、仅靠一次提示词盲写并直接交付像素特效
在特效代码中使用 Math.random()、平滑矢量渐变、无方向光照或未清理的单次残留像素
直接复刻特定商业游戏的专有角色精灵、商标或受版权保护的美术形象
constraints: 本条目保存 patch-gg/pixelfx 固定提交 5294518ce7c72e48b6100a744596e0acf57f2826 的技能原文、编写规范（docs/AUTHORING.md）、目录（docs/CATALOG.md）与 CLI 工具（tools/）。
运行 tools/render.mjs、tools/act.mjs、tools/check.mjs 需要 Node.js 18+ 及同级 src/ 目录（完整运行源码位于关联素材 demos/materials/pixelfx/source/）；导出 GIF 与 MP4 预览时可选依赖 ffmpeg。
新建特效须先阅读 docs/AUTHORING.md 的契约：角色基准尺寸为 24×38 px（actor: 2），局部原点 (0, 0) 位于脚底或命中点，单次特效在 t = duration 时必须完全清空画布，循环特效必须无缝闭合。
每次起草或修改后必须执行 node tools/render.mjs <id> 查看 contact.png 接触表，至少经历三轮“看图找最差问题 → 修复 → 重渲染”，并用 node tools/check.mjs <id> 通过越界、残留、接缝、随机数与帧耗时检查。

# pixelfx Skill：阅读与使用资料

[结构化条目](../../entries/materials/pixelfx-skill.json) 提供来源、固定版本、六步工作流、适用范围与关联素材；可运行特效库与在线画廊见 [pixelfx 组件库说明](pixelfx.md)。

## 核心方法：代码如泥塑，用接触表迭代

pixelfx Skill 源自 Hugo Duprez 的《[How to make (good) pixel art effects with Claude](https://www.spritefusion.com/blog/how-to-make-good-pixel-art-effects-with-claude)》：一次性提示词写出的像素特效往往粗糙平庸；把代码当作黏土，起草后用 `node tools/render.mjs <id>` 渲染出 16 帧采样接触表（`contact.png`），用视觉读图工具打开审视，挑出最差的一项问题修整并重新渲染，经过至少三轮迭代才能做出有手绘生命力的像素特效。

## 六步工作流

1. **环境检查与接触表冒烟**：在包含 `tools/` 与 `src/` 的工作区（本库已完整保存在 [demos/materials/pixelfx/source/](../../demos/materials/pixelfx/source/README.md)）执行 `node tools/render.mjs fire/torch`，查看生成的 `records/fire/torch/contact.png`。
2. **检索并复用现有特效**：先运行 `node tools/list.mjs <关键词>` 或查阅 [CATALOG.md](../../demos/materials/pixelfx-skill/docs/CATALOG.md)。多数需求可通过现有特效配合 `palette`（27 套内置 `PAL` 色板或自定义色值）、`seed`、`flip`、`angle`、`light` 及特效专属 `meta.options` 直接完成：
   ```powershell
   node tools/render.mjs fire/torch --opts '{"palette":["#102","#215","#43a","#8cf","#cff","#fff"]}'
   ```
3. **接入游戏或导出精灵表**：Web/Canvas 游戏直接调用 `createFrame`、`createFx`/`createAct` 与 `composite`；Godot、Unity、Phaser 等引擎执行 `node tools/render.mjs <id> --sheet`（或含角色演出的 `node tools/act.mjs <id> --sheet`）导出透明 PNG 网格与 Aseprite JSON。
4. **确立美术方向并研读参考**：新建特效前先读 [AUTHORING.md](../../demos/materials/pixelfx-skill/docs/AUTHORING.md)，用一句话明确形态、运动、色板与节奏，再阅读库中最接近的 2–3 个特效源码及三个质量标杆（`melee/sword-slash`、`ice/frost-nova`、`explosions/small-explosion`）。
5. **多稿起草与接触表修整循环**：用 `node tools/new.mjs <category>/<name>` 创建模板（方向开放时可并行起草 `-a` 至 `-e` 多稿并渲染对比），打开 `contact.png` 逐轮修正最明显的问题。
6. **编排角色 Act 与自动校验**：涉及角色的特效补充 `export const act`（负时间蓄力前摇、释放帧剪影突变、命中定格 `stop`、震屏 `shake`、草靶受击与收招恢复），用 `node tools/act.mjs <id>` 检查连续 12fps 姿态步进，最后用 `node tools/check.mjs <id>` 确保无画布越界、无尾帧残留、无循环接缝、无 `Math.random()` 且姿态合法。

## 常见视觉缺陷与修整对照

| 接触表或预览中看到的问题 | 修整方法 |
| --- | --- |
| 1× 尺寸下糊成一团 | 减少颜色数量，强化外轮廓剪影，只保留一个视觉焦点，放大主形状。 |
| 形状内部出现孤立噪点像素 | 降低噪声阈值，用 `at()` 量化采样，不在小尺寸形状上叠加噪声。 |
| 动作发飘、缺乏打击感 | 采用快进慢出缓动（`ease.outQuart` / `outExpo`），加入 1–2 帧纯白爆发主帧，缩短总时长。 |
| 运动僵硬机械 | 为每个粒子随机化尺寸、速度、延迟与寿命，补充火花、烟雾、碎屑等次级运动。 |
| 画面过曝泛白 | 降低发光系数（`k` 取 0.2–0.5），压暗边缘色阶，仅在最热核心使用纯白。 |
| 体积扁平无立体感 | 统一单侧受光（左上亮、右下暗），在底部贴地处压暗一档色阶。 |
| 出现矢量式平滑渐变 | `color` 缓冲保持硬色阶过渡，仅在 `light` 发光缓冲与半透明烟雾中使用柔和衰减。 |
| 烟雾呈现棋盘格抖动感 | 改用真正半透明并带顶部受光的 `SMOKE`、`VAPOUR`、`DUST` 粒子或 `p.disc`。 |
| 循环首尾出现跳帧接缝 | 使用 `cycle`、`loopNoise(phase)`、整格 `tileNoise` 滚动或 `sin(phase * TAU * n)`。 |
| 单次特效结束时突然消失 | 在 `t = duration` 前让形状缩小、Bayer 抖动淡出或落入地面以下。 |
| 特效华丽但角色呆若木鸡 | 补充 `act`：与发力反方向的蓄力前摇、释放帧大幅姿态变化、0.03–0.2s 命中定格、受击靶反馈与收招。 |

## 原文入口

- [SKILL.md](../../demos/materials/pixelfx-skill/SKILL.md)：技能主文档，包含检索、接入、导出、新建循环与缺陷对照表。
- [AUTHORING.md](../../demos/materials/pixelfx-skill/docs/AUTHORING.md)：Simulated 与 Pure 特效契约、双缓冲 Painter API、粒子工具箱与 3D 骨骼 Act 规范。
- [CATALOG.md](../../demos/materials/pixelfx-skill/docs/CATALOG.md)：21 个分类下 244 个特效的完整目录。
- [README.md](../../demos/materials/pixelfx-skill/README.md)：上游项目说明。
- [tools/render.mjs](../../demos/materials/pixelfx-skill/tools/render.mjs)、[tools/act.mjs](../../demos/materials/pixelfx-skill/tools/act.mjs)、[tools/check.mjs](../../demos/materials/pixelfx-skill/tools/check.mjs)：接触表渲染、动作步进渲染与质量校验脚本。
- [LICENSES.md](../../demos/materials/pixelfx-skill/LICENSES.md)：MIT 许可与上游署名索引。

# pixelfx

Pixel art effects as code. Each effect is one file, `src/fx/<category>/<name>.js`, that draws into two buffers:
**color** (pixels: opaque, dithered or truly translucent) and **light** (additive glow). No images, so an effect
can be played live, recolored, mirrored, reseeded and rendered to a sprite sheet for any engine.

The method is Hugo Duprez's ([How to make (good) pixel art effects with
Claude](https://www.spritefusion.com/blog/how-to-make-good-pixel-art-effects-with-claude)): code is clay, trust
your eyes, feed your references. One-shot prompts make mediocre effects. Drafts you render, look at and refine
make good ones.

## Before anything

1. Work in a pixelfx checkout. If the working directory has no `tools/render.mjs`, clone one next to the
   project: `git clone https://github.com/patch-gg/pixelfx`. No install step: the tools use only Node.
2. Check it runs: `node tools/render.mjs fire/torch` writes `records/fire/torch/contact.png`. Open that PNG with
   your image-reading tool. That contact sheet is how you see every effect from now on.

## 1. Look for an existing effect first

`node tools/list.mjs <words>` searches ids, names, tags and descriptions (`node tools/list.mjs frost`,
`node tools/list.mjs slash loop`). `docs/CATALOG.md` lists everything by category. Render the candidates and
look at them before choosing. Most requests are an existing effect with different options:

- `palette`: the main ramp, dark to bright, as hex strings. Any `PAL` ramp in `src/core/color.js` (fire ember
  lava smoke dust ice water electric volt poison holy heal arcane shadow blood earth stone gold leaf wood metal
  bone neon cyber matrix candy night) or your own. A blue fire is `{"palette": PAL.ice}`.
- `seed` for a different but equivalent take; `flip` to face left; `angle` to rotate; `light` (0..1+) for glow
  strength; plus each effect's own knobs in its `meta.options` (size, count, radius, text, height...).
- Try options without editing code: `node tools/render.mjs fire/torch --opts '{"palette":["#102","#215","#43a","#8cf","#fff"]}'`.

## 2. Put it in the game

**Canvas or WebGL games in JS or TS** (plain canvas, Phaser, PixiJS, Kaplay, three.js): use the code directly. It
has no dependencies; copy `src/core` and the effect files you need, or depend on the repo.

```js
import { createFrame, clearFrame, createFx, composite } from "pixelfx";   // src/core/index.js
import * as frostNova from "pixelfx/fx/ice/frost-nova";                   // src/fx/ice/frost-nova.js

const frame = createFrame(320, 180);            // the game's pixel resolution; ox, oy scroll it with the camera
const img = new ImageData(320, 180);
const fx = createFx(frostNova, { x: hero.x, y: hero.y, flip: hero.facing < 0 });

// every tick
fx.update(dt);
clearFrame(frame);
fx.draw(frame, "back");    // what goes behind characters
drawCharacters();          // your own sprites, or draw them into frame.color yourself
fx.draw(frame, "front");
composite(frame, img.data, background);   // color over the background plus light; or null for transparent
ctx.putImageData(img, 0, 0);              // then scale the canvas up with image-rendering: pixelated
if (fx.done()) removeIt();               // one-shots end on their own; fx.stop() fades a loop out
```

Several effects can share one frame. In a WebGL engine, upload the composited RGBA to a texture each frame, or
render the effect to a sprite sheet once (below) and play it like any other animation.

**Any engine** (Godot, Unity, GameMaker, Defold, LÖVE, Bevy, Construct): export sprite sheets.
`node tools/render.mjs ice/frost-nova --sheet` writes `records/ice/frost-nova/frost-nova.png` (transparent
frames in a grid) and `frost-nova.json` (Aseprite-style frames, so Phaser's atlas loader, Godot and Unity Aseprite
importers and most tools read it; `meta.pixelfx` has fps, loop, frame size, columns and the pivot). Set the
pivot to `meta.pixelfx.pivot` (the effect's origin, e.g. the feet), import with nearest-neighbour filtering and no
compression, and play at `meta.pixelfx.fps`. Glow is baked into the sheet as color with alpha, which reads as
additive over dark scenes; for bright scenes, render a recolored version or keep the effect on a dark layer.

For the full library: `node tools/render.mjs <category> --sheet` does a whole category.

**A hit needs a body behind it.** An effect alone looks like a sticker. Effects with a character carry an `act`: when the body winds
up, when to freeze, how the target reacts. Use it whichever way the game is built:

- With the stock character: `createAct(slash, { x, y })` instead of `createFx`. `act.update(dt)`, `act.draw(frame)`, and throw the
  picture by `act.shake`. It holds still by itself during a freeze. `node tools/act.mjs <id> --sheet` bakes the lot into a sprite sheet.
- With the game's own character: read the timing, `slash.act` or `meta.pixelfx.act` in a sheet's JSON (`windup`, `recovery`, `hits`
  with `t` and `freeze`). Play the character's attack animation `windup` seconds before the effect, and at each hit stop updating
  everything, effect and characters both, for `freeze` seconds. Host-side hit-stop works on any effect, with or without an act.

`src/fx/moves/` has whole attacks chained from the effects, wind-up to recovery: start there when someone asks for a move, not an effect.

## 3. Make a new one

Read `docs/AUTHORING.md` first: it is the contract (meta, `draw(p, t, o)` for pure effects or `create(o)` for
simulated ones, local coordinates, seamless loops, ending empty), the toolkit, the painter API and the quality bar.
Then:

1. **Say it in one line** with art direction: what it is, how it moves, its palette, its timing. "A frost nova:
   crystals erupt in a ring from the feet outward, a white flash at the center, shards spin off, the floor stays
   frosted and fades."
2. **Find references** in the library: `node tools/list.mjs <words>`, then read the two or three closest effect
   files and borrow their techniques (`Particles` and `Bits` in `src/core/sim.js` for sparks, smoke and debris,
   `p.disc` for translucent volumes, `cycle` for seamless particles, `tileFbm` scrolls for flames and water). Look at
   the closest of [Hugo Duprez's effects](https://www.spritefusion.com/pixel-art-vfx) too: they are the quality bar.
   If his has more detail, light or life at the same size on screen, yours isn't done.
3. **Draft.** `node tools/new.mjs <category>/<name>` (add `--loop` for a loop) gives a working file. When the
   direction is open, write 3 to 5 genuinely different drafts (`<name>-a.js` .. `-e.js`), render them all
   (`node tools/render.mjs "<category>/<name>-*"`) and look at every contact sheet before choosing. Show the user
   the strongest two or three if they're around (`--gif` makes animations to share).
4. **Look, judge, fix.** Render, open `records/<id>/contact.png`, and judge like a picky pixel artist. Fix the
   worst thing, render again. Three rounds minimum; a showpiece takes more. `--all` shows every frame,
   `--mp4` shows motion at full speed.
5. **Act it out** if a character is involved: add `export const act` (see "Acts" in `docs/AUTHORING.md`), with a wind-up before t = 0,
   a pose change on the release frame, a freeze on contact and a recovery. `node tools/act.mjs <id>` shows consecutive 12 fps steps:
   judge motion from those and from `--mp4`, not from a contact sheet's samples.
6. **Check.** `node tools/check.mjs <id>` catches drawing outside the canvas, one-shots that don't end empty,
   loop seams, unseeded randomness and slow frames, and in an act: keys out of order, unknown pose fields and hands
   that teleport. Fix until it passes clean. Delete the drafts you didn't keep.

What to look for, and the usual fix:

| you see | fix |
|---|---|
| it reads as mush at 1x | fewer colors, a clear silhouette, one focal point, bigger shapes |
| speckle: lone noise pixels inside shapes | threshold noise less, quantize with `at()`, no noise on small shapes |
| floaty, no punch | fast in, slow out (`ease.outQuart`/`outExpo`), a 1 to 2 frame white hero frame, shorter total time |
| stiff or mechanical | vary every particle (size, speed, delay, life), add secondary motion (sparks, smoke, debris) |
| washed out | less glow (k 0.2 to 0.5), darker edge steps, keep white for the hottest core only |
| flat | light from one side: brighter top-left, darker bottom-right step; a darker ramp step at the base |
| smooth gradients, vector look | hard ramp steps in color; softness only in light and in translucent smoke |
| a checkerboard where smoke should be | `SMOKE`, `VAPOUR` or `DUST` particles, or `p.disc`: truly translucent, lit on top |
| seam when a loop wraps | `cycle`, `loopNoise(phase)`, whole-cell `tileNoise` scrolls, `sin(phase * TAU * n)` |
| a one-shot that pops off | let it shrink, dither out or fall away before t = duration |
| a great effect on a dead character | give it an act: wind-up, release pose, freeze on contact, a target that reacts, recovery |
| the act feels weightless | a wind-up the opposite way to the blow, a longer freeze (up to 0.2 s), a bigger silhouette change, shake |
| the hit lands out of sync | move the hit key to the effect's own constant, not to a time you eyeballed |
| he holds the weapon badly | keep a bend in the elbow, shafts in front of the chest; on a swing the blade lags the hand; arms reach about 15 px and don't stretch, so step the body in |
| his arms cross or the pose looks flat | he faces three-quarters towards us: for open arms the near hand goes left (`fx < 0`), far hand right, with `turn: 1`; `yaw` really turns him |

Directional effects face right, ground effects stand on y = 0, actor effects wrap `o.actor` (a 24 x 38 stock
character's mask and pixels), and nothing uses `Math.random`. Generic motifs are fine; never recreate a specific game's
sprites, characters or logos.

## 4. Native code instead of JS

If the game can't run JS and a sprite sheet isn't enough (an effect that follows a moving target, or needs
per-instance colors at runtime), port the effect. Pure effects are a function of time; simulated ones step the particles in
`src/core/sim.js`. Keep the two-buffer idea, the 4x4 Bayer threshold for dithered alpha and the palette ramp lookups.
Render the JS original and your port side by side to check they match.

# Writing an effect

An effect is one file, `src/fx/<category>/<name>.js` (kebab-case), drawing pixel art over time into two buffers.
It has no images and no dependencies beyond `src/core`. It can be played live, recolored, mirrored and rendered
to a sprite sheet for any engine.

The quality bar is Sprite Fusion's open-source pixel art VFX by Hugo Duprez
([spritefusion.com/pixel-art-vfx](https://www.spritefusion.com/pixel-art-vfx), MIT). Every effect here should hold up
next to his at the same size on screen: as much detail, as much light, as much life. `src/core/sim.js` is adapted
from his code; read the three references written to that bar first: `src/fx/melee/sword-slash.js`,
`src/fx/ice/frost-nova.js`, `src/fx/explosions/small-explosion.js`.

## Two kinds of effect

**Simulated** (most one-shots: impacts, explosions, spells, anything with debris, sparks, smoke or fire). Export
`create(o)` returning `{ update(dt), draw(p), drawBack?(p) }`. Spawn particles, debris and lights in `create` and
`update`, keep your own `t`, draw from state. The runtime steps it at 120 Hz or finer, so physics looks the same at
any frame rate. Use the seeded `Rng` from `o.seed` for every random number.

```js
import { Particles, Lights, P, PF, Rng, fit, sparkle, smooth } from "../../core/index.js";

export const meta = { name: "Spark pop", desc: "...", tags: ["impact"], size: [96, 72], origin: [48, 56],
  duration: 1.2, loop: false, fps: 30, bg: "ground", options: { palette: [...], seed: 1 } };

export function create(o) {
  const C = fit(o.palette, 7), R = new Rng(o.seed), floor = () => 0;
  const ps = new Particles({ rng: R, ground: floor }), lights = new Lights();
  lights.add(0, -12, 40, C[4], 0.7, 0.4);
  for (let i = 0; i < 40; i++) {
    const a = R.range(0, Math.PI * 2), sp = R.range(80, 260);
    ps.spawn(P.SPARK, 0, -12, Math.cos(a) * sp, Math.sin(a) * sp - 60, R.range(0.2, 0.6));
  }
  let t = 0;
  return {
    update(dt) { t += dt; ps.update(dt); lights.update(dt); },
    draw(p) { if (t < 0.12) sparkle(p, 0, -12, 9 * (1 - t / 0.12), C[5], C[3]); ps.draw(p); lights.draw(p); },
  };
}
```

**Pure** (loops, and shapes that are a function of time: auras, portals, waterfalls, beams, critters). Export
`draw(p, t, o)` (and `drawBack(p, t, o)`): the frame at `t` from `t` alone, so it loops with no seam. Particles
that loop come from `cycle`, motion from `fly`, noise from `loopNoise`/`tileFbm`.

## The contract

- **Scale.** The stock character is 24 x 38 px (`actor: 2`): every effect is drawn at that scale, detail at the
  1 px level. Canvases are as big as the effect needs, often 96 to 320 px wide; transitions are 320 x 180.
- **Local coordinates.** (0, 0) is the anchor: the feet of the character, the point of impact, the base of a
  torch, the muzzle. x right, y down, 1 unit = 1 px. The painter places, mirrors (`flip`) and rotates (`angle`).
  Directional effects face right. Ground effects stand on y = 0, the floor; floor rings, cracks, scorch and
  puddles may draw a little below it as perspective.
- **Time.** One-shots run 0..duration and draw **nothing at t = duration** (set duration long enough for the last
  smoke to clear). Loops are seamless.
- **Options** `o`: `meta.options` merged with the caller's. Honour `o.palette` (main ramp, dark to bright; use
  `fit(o.palette, n)` so any length works) and `o.seed`. Other color ramps as options are resampled too.
  `x`, `y`, `flip`, `angle`, `light` are reserved.
- **Deterministic.** Never `Math.random()` or `Date`.
- **Layers.** `drawBack` for what's behind a character or the far half of a ring; `draw` for the rest.
- **Actor effects** (`actor: 2`) get `o.actor = { mask, pixels, x, y, w, h, head, chest }`: the character's
  silhouette and its own colors (`pixels`, a Uint32Array, 0 where empty) in local space, feet at (0, 0). Recolor
  `pixels` for frozen, poisoned, stone; outline `mask` for auras. Export `actorAlpha(t, o)` (0..1) when the
  character should vanish or appear; previews follow it.
- **Acts** (`export const act`): what the body does around the effect. Any effect with a character should have one; see
  below.
- **Credit.** If you adapt a specific recipe from one of Hugo's files, put a two-line credit at the top of yours:
  `// ... adapted from Sprite Fusion's open-source <name> (https://www.spritefusion.com/pixel-art-vfx/<name>),`
  `// MIT License, Copyright (c) 2026 Hugo Duprez.`

## Acts

An effect shows what the magic does. Its act shows what the character does. Without one, the best effect looks like a
sticker on a mannequin. Replies to the first release said it best: "lack of anticipation and cooldown phases".

```js
const GUARD = { ...READY, weapon: "sword", fx: 12, fy: -19, sa: -0.75 };
const COCK = { ...GUARD, crouch: 4, lean: -4, fx: -9, fy: -33, sa: -2.7, bx: 9, by: -22, armsFront: true };
const CUT = { ...GUARD, crouch: 4, lean: 5, fx: 24, fy: -19, sa: 0.6, ffx: 13, fbx: -10, ghost: 1 };

export const act = {
  target: { x: 58 },                                // or targets: [{ x: 58 }, { x: 104 }]
  poses: [[-0.5, GUARD], [-0.2, COCK], [0.06, CUT, "snap"], [0.7, GUARD]],
  hits: [{ t: 0.06, stop: 0.14, shake: 0.18, amp: 2, push: 2.8, straw: 18, skin: "char" }],
  dust: [{ t: 0.06, x: 12, n: 6, dir: 1 }],
};
```

- **Time** is the effect's own: t = 0 is its first frame, so a negative key is a wind-up. A one-shot's act runs to its last
  key, which may be after the effect has ended. A loop's keys run 0 to `duration` and match at both ends.
- **Poses** only say what differs from standing easy. `src/core/poses.js` lists every field and how the body works: where the feet and
  hands are, crouch, lean, turn, what's held and at what angle. The character is a real skeleton in 3D, drawn down to pixels: hands and
  feet are placed where they should end up, in px from the feet, and elbows, knees, spine and shoulders work themselves out. Between keys, limbs step at 12 fps and the feet's position stays smooth.
  `"snap"` holds the last pose and jumps on the key, `"out"` arrives fast and settles, `"in"` starts slow, `"line"` keeps a
  steady speed.
- **Hits** freeze everything for `stop` seconds and shake it by `amp` px for `shake` seconds; the target takes `push` (negative
  rocks it towards the caster), `straw`, `flash`, a `skin` (char, ice, shock, holy, shadow, red, poison; `null` clears it) and `shiver`.
  `at` picks one of several targets; `target: false` leaves them out of it. Line these up with the effect's own constants.
- **Weapons** are `sword greatsword dagger spear hammer scythe claw bow pistol launcher handle`. `two: true` puts both hands on it.
- **Hold it like you mean it.** An arm reaches about 15 px from its shoulder and bones don't stretch, so step the body (`x`) rather than ask too much,
  and keep a little bend in the elbow. On a swing the blade lags the hand: at mid-swing the arm has gone forward while the blade still points up, so the
  wrist breaks and it whips. Weapons stop at the floor by themselves. A long weapon rests in one hand, butt on the floor, and takes the second hand to swing.
- **Use the third dimension.** He faces right, three-quarters towards us, so for arms raised or open the near hand goes left of the chest (`fx < 0`) and the
  far hand right (`bx > 0`), usually with `turn: 1` so the chest faces us. `yaw` turns the whole body about its feet, weapon included: a spin is really a spin.
- **Line the hand up** with where the effect fires from: if a beam leaves `(15, -24)`, the pose's `fx, fy` are `15, -24` at t = 0.
- **`onBody: true`** when the effect reads `o.actor` (recolors `pixels`, outlines `mask`, exports `actorAlpha`). Draw it against the
  standing body as usual: each pixel of a pose knows which standing pixel it came from, so frost, poison and scan lines follow. What's
  off the body moves with the chest above the belt and stays put on the floor; `follow: 0` keeps it fixed, for a core at the hand.
- **What sells it:** a wind-up in the opposite direction to the blow. A big silhouette change on the release frame. A freeze
  on contact, longer for heavier blows (0.03 to 0.2 s). A follow-through that overshoots. Sword tips and hammer heads that meet the effect's arc.
  Raised hands go behind the head by themselves, so the face stays visible; put wind-ups beside or above the head, not across it.

**Moves** (`src/fx/moves/`) are effects made of effects. `chain` plays other effects as cues; a projectile is an effect whose `x`
is a function of time; `shiftKeys` reuses other effects' acts.

```js
export const create = chain([
  { fx: charge, t: 0.08, until: THROW, palette: PAL.fire },
  { fx: fireball, t: THROW, until: HIT, x: (t) => 28 + (t - THROW) * SPEED, y: -22 },
  { fx: blast, t: HIT, x: TX },
]);
```

Judge acts by their motion: `node tools/act.mjs <id>` shows consecutive 12 fps steps, `--mp4` plays it, and `tools/check.mjs` catches keys out of
order, unknown pose fields, loop seams and hands that teleport.

## The toolkit (`src/core/sim.js`, from Sprite Fusion's code)

- `new Particles({ rng, ground: (x) => floorY, sparks: [head..tail colors], haze: color, onLand })`,
  `ps.spawn(kind, x, y, vx, vy, life, color, size, delay, flags)`, `ps.update(dt)`, `ps.draw(p, "back"|"front")`.
  Kinds `P.*`: `SPARK` (speed-stretched two-tone streak, gravity, bounces on the floor, glows), `MOTE` (streak
  with a dark tail, dithers out), `STREAK` (accelerating dotted line: gathering energy), `FLAKE` (drifting
  speck, a cross when big), `VAPOUR` (soft translucent puff that swells and thins, optional haze glow), `DUST`
  (denser puff), `SMOKE` (three soft discs, lit cap, rises and sways; color 0 uses `SMOKE_RAMP`), `FIRE`
  (a ball of flame cooling down `FIRE_RAMP` as it rises; flag `PF.SMOKES` turns it to smoke when it dies,
  `PF.BIG` for bigger slower smoke), `BRAND` (burning chunk that trails flame and calls `onLand`), `GRIT`
  (falling bits that bounce once and settle), `EMBER` (rising, wandering, cooling), `STAR` (twinkling cross).
  `PF.BACK` draws a particle behind. `delay` holds it back.
- `new Bits({ ground })`, `bits.add({ kind: B.SHARD|B.CHUNK|B.DRIP, x, y, vx, vy, a, va, s, c, ramp, g, drag,
  bounce, life })`: rigid debris that tumbles, bounces and settles (`rest`).
- `new Lights()`, `lights.add(x, y, r, color, k, life)`: lights that flare and die (k falls with life²).
- `new Blazes(ps)`, `blazes.add(x, y, life, power)`: small fires that keep feeding flame where something landed.
- `sparkle(p, x, y, arm, c, tip, k)` star glint; `flare(p, x, y, L, k, ramp)` 8-ray flare;
  `band(p, cx, cy, r, sy, thick, alpha, ramp, keep, hot)` a ring on a tilted plane (sy 0.16 lies on the floor;
  keep `(g) => Math.sin(g) < 0` is the far half); `crystal(p, x, base, h, w, lean, ramp, { a, white, glint })` a
  faceted ice/crystal spike with a lit ridge.
- `GRAVITY` = 950 px/s². Hugo's code uses world units (2 per px): halve his speeds, distances and gravity.

## The bar

What makes Sprite Fusion's effects good, and what every effect here must do:

1. **Lines and light, not fills.** Build with 1 px rims, rings, trails and sparks, and let light carry the
   brightness. A big flat area of saturated color is almost always wrong. White-hot cores and edges, tinted
   middles, deep color only in shadow.
2. **Light everywhere.** A big soft pool at low k, a tight hot one at the core, a light on every spark and
   glint, `Lights` that flare at the moment of impact and fall away, light along arcs and beams, a warm or cold
   pool on the floor while something burns or freezes.
3. **Translucent volumes.** Smoke, vapour, dust and mist are soft (`SMOKE`, `VAPOUR`, `DUST`, `p.disc`), lit on
   top, swelling and thinning. Never a dithered checkerboard for smoke.
4. **Real motion.** Sparks stretch with speed, fall and bounce. Debris tumbles, bounces, settles and fades.
   Fire rises and cools into smoke. Things that land kick up dust. Use drag: fast burst, slow drift.
5. **Choreography in phases.** Anticipation or charge (things gathering in), release (a 1 to 2 frame white
   hero frame, a flare, light, a burst), spread, hold (twinkles, glints, embers), break or melt, a long decay.
   Many small events, each varied in size, speed, timing and life.
6. **Depth.** Rings on the floor are flat ellipses with a far half behind the character and a near half in
   front. Back rows of crystals or flames are dimmer.
7. **Timing.** Fast attack, slow release. Big effects linger 2 to 4 s while smoke clears and sparkles fade;
   hits are snappy (0.3 to 0.8 s) but still have follow-through.
8. **Reads at 1x** with a clear focal point, no speckle noise inside shapes.
9. **Original.** Generic motifs fine; never a specific game's sprite, character or logo. Don't copy one of
   Hugo's effects wholesale: use his techniques, make the design your own.
10. **Clean.** Fits its canvas, ends empty or loops clean, deterministic, under 2 ms a frame (`tools/check.mjs`).

## The method

The method is Hugo Duprez's ([How to make (good) pixel art effects with
Claude](https://www.spritefusion.com/blog/how-to-make-good-pixel-art-effects-with-claude)): code is clay, trust
your eyes, feed your references.

1. **Reference first.** Find the closest of [his effects](https://www.spritefusion.com/pixel-art-vfx), look at it, and
   read its source for the choreography and numbers. His code uses world units, 2 per pixel.
2. **Say it in one line** with the art direction, then draft.
3. **Render and look**: `node tools/render.mjs <id> --zoom 3` (contact sheet in `records/<id>/contact.png`;
   `--all` every frame, `--mp4` motion).
4. **Benchmark**: put his and yours next to each other at the same height on screen. If his has more detail, light
   or life, yours isn't done.
5. **Fix the worst thing, render again.** Three rounds minimum; showpieces take more.
6. **Act it out** if there's a character: `node tools/act.mjs <id>`. Consecutive frames, not samples.
7. **Check**: `node tools/check.mjs <id>` until it passes clean.
